meta.status: 2026 statutory and unemployment-insurance figures from primary government sources; wages (BLS QCEW 2025), health (AHRQ MEPS-IC 2025) and workers' comp index (Oregon DCBS 2024) are the latest published editions, labeled with their own years. Fields without a 2026 primary source say so and carry a low-confidence flag.

sources.name: Social Security Administration — Contribution and benefit base
Federal Register 2026-00342 — FUTA credit reductions applicable for 2025
U.S. Department of Labor, ETA Office of Unemployment Insurance — Significant Provisions of State UI Laws, effective July 2026
State workforce agencies (DC, MD, VA, CA, TX, FL, NY, OH) — see each state's sui_source
Oregon Department of Consumer and Business Services — 2024 Oregon Workers' Compensation Premium Rate Ranking (published 2025)
U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics — Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages (QCEW), 2025 annual averages, private ownership
AHRQ Medical Expenditure Panel Survey — Insurance Component (MEPS-IC) 2025, private sector, state tables II.B.2.b, II.C.1, II.C.2, II.D.1, II.D.2

federal.futa_credit_reduction_note: California: 1.2% applied for 2025 (Federal Register 2026-00342). For 2026 the statutory schedule adds 0.3 points (1.5%) if the state still owes Title XII advances on Nov. 10, 2026; DOL finalizes after that date. Estimate until then.

fica_rates.note: Statutory: 6.2% Social Security (26 U.S.C. 3111(a)), 1.45% Medicare (3111(b)). Employer pays no Additional Medicare Tax.

futa.note: Statutory: 6.0% on the first $7,000 (26 U.S.C. 3301, 3306(b)(1)) less the maximum 5.4% state credit = 0.6% net.

health.source: AHRQ MEPS-IC 2025, United States, private sector: average single premium minus average employee contribution (Tables II.C.1, II.C.2).

peo_admin.note: Practitioner-derived market ranges for full-service PEO, 10-100 EE tier.

wc_industry_multipliers.note: PEOnomics estimate (not a published source): approximate class-mix exposure relative to the Oregon index basket. Use your class-code rate or quote whenever you have it.

hr_admin_burden.source: PwC, 'The hidden reality of payroll & HR administration costs' (2011, ADP-sponsored). Dollar figures CPI-adjusted ~+43% to 2026.
hr_admin_burden.note: In-house TCO of payroll, workforce admin, time & attendance, and H&W administration, per employee per year. Hidden costs (indirect labor, seams, system maintenance) are >50% of this per the study. Smaller employers pay more PEPY due to diseconomies of scale; tiers below extrapolate the study's size curve and are labeled as estimates.
